report_name: 'FaceHugger' Flaws in Hugging Face Diffusers Bypass Security Controls

attack_patterns.name: AI Supply Chain Compromise: Model
attack_patterns.description: A malicious AI model is used as the vector to compromise a developer's system by exploiting vulnerabilities in the Hugging Face Diffusers library.

attack_patterns.name: Machine Compromise: AI Artifacts
attack_patterns.description: A malicious AI model artifact, when loaded by the Diffusers library, executes arbitrary code on the host machine, leading to a full system compromise.

attack_patterns.name: Masquerading
attack_patterns.description: The CVE-2026-44827 vulnerability involves using a specifically named file, 'None.py', to masquerade as a legitimate component and bypass security checks in the Diffusers library.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Python
attack_patterns.description: The arbitrary code executed by the malicious model runs within the context of the Python process that loaded the vulnerable Diffusers library.

malware.name: FaceHugger Poisoned Model
malware.description: A maliciously crafted AI model that exploits 'FaceHugger' vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-44513, CVE-2026-44827, CVE-2026-45804) in the Hugging Face Diffusers library to execute arbitrary code on the host machine.

tools.name: Hugging Face Diffusers
tools.description: A popular open-source library for generative AI models. Versions prior to 0.38.0 contain the 'FaceHugger' vulnerabilities, which allow for arbitrary code execution when loading a malicious model.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-44513
vulnerabilities.description: A code injection flaw in Hugging Face Diffusers where the custom_pipeline feature can be abused to load and execute code even when trust_remote_code is set to false.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-44827
vulnerabilities.description: A code injection bug in Hugging Face Diffusers where a repository containing a file named None.py is not properly checked by the security mechanism, allowing its code to be executed.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-45804
vulnerabilities.description: A race condition in Hugging Face Diffusers where a model repository's configuration can be modified between cloning and loading, leading to malicious code execution.

identities.name: Hugging Face
identities.description: Vendor of the vulnerable Diffusers library and operator of the Hugging Face Hub model repository, which is a key part of the described AI supply chain.

identities.name: AI Developers and Researchers
identities.description: The primary group of users targeted by the FaceHugger vulnerabilities, as they use the Diffusers library to load and work with AI models from public repositories.

infrastructure.name: Malicious Model on Hugging Face Hub
infrastructure.description: A malicious AI model repository published on the Hugging Face Hub, designed to exploit FaceHugger vulnerabilities in the Diffusers library upon being loaded by a developer.

indicators.name: FaceHugger Exploit Artifact None.py
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: FaceHugger Exploit Artifact None.py
id: 2f8b1c9a-4e7d-4f6a-8b3c-9d1e0f2a3b4c
status: experimental
description: Detects the presence of a file named 'None.py' within a downloaded Hugging Face model repository, which is a strong indicator of an attempt to exploit CVE-2026-44827.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/hugging-face-diffusers-flaws-could-let.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-04
tags:
  - attack.aml.t0074
  - attack.defense_evasion
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\None.py'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of a file named 'None.py', a specific indicator for the exploitation of CVE-2026-44827 ('FaceHugger').

indicators.name: Suspicious Shell Spawning from Python Process
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Shell Spawning from Python Process
id: 8c9d0e1f-2a3b-4c5d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f
status: experimental
description: Detects a Python process spawning a command shell, which could indicate arbitrary code execution from a malicious AI model like those exploiting FaceHugger vulnerabilities.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/hugging-face-diffusers-flaws-could-let.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-04
tags:
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.execution
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\pythonw.exe'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects a Python process, potentially after loading an AI model, spawning a command shell, which is a strong indicator of arbitrary code execution.

indicators.name: Suspicious Outbound Connection from Python Model Loading Process
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Outbound Connection from Python Process
id: 5a6b7c8d-9e0f-4a1b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects unexpected outbound network connections from a Python process, which could indicate a malicious payload from an AI model communicating with a C2 server after exploiting a vulnerability like FaceHugger.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/hugging-face-diffusers-flaws-could-let.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-04
tags:
  - attack.t1071
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\pythonw.exe'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
    Initiated: true
  filter_local:
    DestinationIp|in:
      - '127.0.0.1'
      - '::1'
  filter_known_repo:
    DestinationHostname|endswith:
      - '.huggingface.co'
      - '.python.org'
      - '.pypi.org'
  condition: selection and not filter_local and not filter_known_repo
indicators.description: Detects a Python process making outbound network connections to unknown destinations, a potential sign of a malicious payload communicating with a C2 server.
